Subject: Redlines: Anchored shelf pricing + escape hatch language

Hi Jillian / Tom —

Thanks again for the productive conversation yesterday. Per our call, attaching a redline of the order form and Exhibit B with two items we'd like to resolve before we move to signature:

1) Anchored shelf / floor mechanics: we added language that ties the minimum monthly fee to a graduated floor rather than a single fixed floor for year one. This is intended to give AcmeMed predictability while allowing usage growth to amortize the fee.

2) Escape hatch / clawback trigger: proposed an explicit true-up window and a 60-day cure period before clawback. We kept the financial remittance timing aligned to normal invoicing cycles.

Please see attached Acme_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf and a cleaned pricing schedule (Exhibit-B_pricing_schedule.xlsx). Key asks from our side:
- Confirm whether the proposed graduated floor (table on pg 3 of Exhibit B) is acceptable to Finance.
- If Acme needs a shorter cure window, share the business justification so we can make a commercial trade.

We can schedule 30 minutes tomorrow to walk the redline if that helps — I can bring Karthik and Laura.

Best,
Irene

Thanks, Irene — appreciate the clear summary and the redline. Quick initial read and questions: 

• Graduated floor table looks reasonable from a product usage perspective, but Finance wants to understand the uplift assumptions that justify the year-1 slope. Can you share the forecast or the rationale that led to the buckets?

• On the clawback: AcmeMed legal prefers a 30-day cure window (our billing cadence is monthly and we prefer quicker reconciliation), and they want explicit examples of what constitutes a "material drop" to trigger clawback. Can Redwood provide objective thresholds (e.g., >40% M/M dip) rather than subjective language?

• We also flagged the passthrough for overage credits in Exhibit B — can you confirm whether those credits are applied monthly or on the next invoice period?

I'll loop Finance if we need more detail. Happy to take the walkthrough tomorrow.

Best,
Jillian Park

Jillian / team —

Thanks for the quick read. To help Finance and Legal evaluate, a few datapoints and a proposed compromise on timing: 

1) Forecast rationale: the graduated floor is modeled from Acme's stated 12-month ramp (20% month-over-month for first 4 months, then 10% M/M for next 4, then leveling). We used your intake numbers from the discovery deck and modeled conservative utilization per seat for the shelf SKU. I can drop the modeling spreadsheet into the HubSpot link (or share a Drive link) if that helps.

2) Clawback threshold: we can accept a numeric trigger instead of subjective language. Proposed language: "Clawback may be initiated if actual billed usage falls below 60% of forecasted usage for two consecutive months, measured on an invoice-to-invoice basis." That gives a clear rule and a two-month buffer to avoid transient dips.

3) Cure window: Redwood can shorten the cure window to 45 days (from 60) if Acme can commit to monthly remittance and timely reconciliations. If Acme requires 30 days, we would need to add a small administrative fee to cover potential churned allocation (propose 1.5% of the reclaimed amount).

4) Credits treatment: overage/underage credits are applied on the invoice following the reconciliation month (so a May usage true-up shows on June invoice). We can mark that in Exhibit B language to avoid ambiguity.

If those three points work, I think legal can proceed to finalize. Happy to join a call.

- Karthik
Head of Revenue Strategy, Redwood Inference

Jillian / Tom —

From Legal's perspective a few suggested cleanups to formalize the numeric triggers and timing that Karthik proposed: 

• Replace "material drop" with: "actual billed usage for the relevant SKU falls to less than sixty percent (60%) of the then-current Forecast for two (2) consecutive billing cycles."

• Define "Forecast" in Exhibit B and reference the accepted forecasting spreadsheet as an incorporated reference (e.g., "Forecast means the forecasting table attached as Schedule 1 to Exhibit B"). That prevents disputes about which numbers govern.

• Cure period language: "Customer shall have forty-five (45) days from receipt of a notice of clawback to cure the deficiency by providing usage logs and making any agreed payment adjustments; failing which Seller may invoice for the reclaimed amounts."

• Add a short sentence clarifying credit timing: "Any overage or underage credits resulting from reconciliation shall appear on the invoice following the reconciliation month and, if invoiced as a credit, shall be applied to the next invoice due."

I've incorporated these edits into the attached Acme_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (tracked). If this matches Acme's needs on clarity and objectivity, we can push to signature.

Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference

Jillian / Tom —

Thanks for the responses and the proposed changes. Summary of what Redwood is prepared to accept: 

• Numeric clawback trigger: 60% of Forecast for two consecutive billing cycles — accepted.
• Forecast to be attached as Schedule 1 to Exhibit B — accepted. We'll export the modeling tab and attach the conservative view.
• Cure window: accept 45 days — Redwood will not charge the administrative fee if Acme commits to monthly reconciliation and timely evidence submission.
• Credit timing: clarify in Exhibit B that credits appear on the invoice following the reconciliation month.

Next steps: Laura will incorporate the final Schedule 1 (forecast spreadsheet) and re-run page numbering; Karthik will upload the modeling spreadsheet to the HubSpot link. If no further redlines from Acme by EOD Wednesday, let's proceed to DocuSign.

I'll schedule a 30-minute handoff for Thursday to review the final doc.

Best,
Irene
